items.title: Chinese army distributes used briefcases to cut costs — South China Morning Post
items.summary: China’s People’s Liberation Army is cutting costs by distributing used briefcases, reusing equipment parts and decorations, and introducing double-sided printing, SCMP reports.

items.title: Russian forces attacked an industrial facility in Kremenchuk district
items.summary: The head of the Poltava Regional Military Administration reported the strike and said the information was being clarified.

items.title: Yemeni army launches probe into reports of toxic substances in Taiz — Anadolu Agency
items.summary: Yemen’s army is investigating reports that Houthi forces may have used munitions containing toxic substances in Taiz, where attacks and road blockages continue.

items.title: UN Warns of Freezing Winter as Russian Strikes Threaten Ukraine’s Power
items.summary: The UN refugee agency warns that nine million people in Ukraine, Syria, Lebanon and Afghanistan need urgent winter assistance, as Russian attacks on Ukraine’s energy infrastructure threaten heating and electricity supplies.

items.title: Netanyahu bloc wins 53 Knesset seats — Jerusalem Post
items.summary: Netanyahu’s bloc won 53 Knesset seats in Israel’s final election count, while the opposition secured 48. Neither bloc reached the 61-seat majority threshold.

items.title: Likud claims election was allegedly stolen after losing majority — PBS NewsHour
items.summary: Likud claimed without evidence that Israel’s election was stolen after its bloc won 53 of 120 Knesset seats, while the election commission reviews suspicions of foreign interference.

items.title: 10 US military transport aircraft arrive in Israel — Jerusalem Post
items.summary: Ten US Air Force military transport aircraft arrived at air bases in southern Israel as part of a larger convoy, KAN reported.

items.title: Russian Cinema Association Pushes Free Propaganda Screenings for Students
Russian Ballistic Missile Strike on Kyiv Kills One, Sparks Fires
items.summary: Russian ballistic missiles struck Kyiv late Thursday, killing at least one person, setting warehouses ablaze and damaging residential buildings and vehicles in two districts.

items.title: How Big of a Threat Are the Houthis?
items.summary: The Saudi ambassador to the U.S. compared them to the Islamic State.

items.title: Oleshky Aid Convoy Ready to Depart as Demining Is Completed
items.summary: Demining of routes into Russian-occupied Oleshky has been completed, Ukraine’s human rights commissioner Dmytro Lubinets said Thursday evening, Oct. 29, adding that a humanitarian convoy bound for the town’s central hospital is ready to depart. Residents will be able to leave until 2 p.m. local time, until aid distribution begins at 2:30 p.m. A Ukrainian and Russian delegation will observe the mission alongside a US journalistic crew from Newsmax.

items.title: The portraits of dead friends are coming off the walls. After 29 years, Russia’s independent Novaya Gazeta newspaper is being forced out of its Moscow newsroom.
items.summary: Novaya Gazeta will be evicted from its office on Potapovsky Lane in central Moscow, where it has been based for 29 years, the news outlet Ekho reported. Ekho cited a letter to readers from editor-in-chief Sergey Sokolov and journalist Irina Gordiyenko.

items.title: Residents of Russian-occupied Oleshky have until Friday afternoon to leave. Aid distribution for those who stay is scheduled to begin under a temporary ceasefire.
items.summary: Routes for a humanitarian mission in Oleshky, in Ukraine’s Kherson region, have been cleared of mines. Russian and Ukrainian human rights commissioners Yana Lantratova and Dmytro Lubinets said the humanitarian convoy is ready to depart.

items.title: Saudi Civil Defence reports that debris fell in Riyadh following the interception of two ballistic missiles.
